items.title: 68642_Jo Jones oral history interview
items.q: stayed there 30 weeks with Jimmy Jones's band.

ctx.x: And the second one was your daughter. What's her name?

Joanne. When my first was born, Milt, I was making $5 a week with comebacks. You know what a comeback is? All right, now I'm going to tell you something. I have it in my scrapbook. We were working at the Peacock Inn at 19th and Farnum; stayed there 30 weeks with Jimmy Jones's band. Now we were making we started out at thought around $35 a week. We begin to get letters from Ben Webster, from Paul Webster, from Basie, from everybody.
* a tip, money in the kitty

items.title: 69537_Jimmy Jones oral history interview
items.q: Jo Jones was playing drums. Roy Eldridge was playing trumpet

ctx.x: I think that was one on the tape where the sound level was off, so tell me about that record date again.

That's the one. I think Ray Brown was playing bass, I was playing piano. Jo Jones was playing drums. Roy Eldridge was playing trumpet, and that's the one where Ben Webster called up Norman Granz. We'd had a record date the day before. He called him up, he says, "Can you find the old man for me?" He's talking about Coleman Hawkins now.
